title: Emerging Roles of TMEM97/Sigma-2 Receptor in Breast Cancer Endocrine Resistance: Links to mTOR Signaling and Cholesterol Metabolism
content: Breast cancer is one of the most common cancers in women, and the majority of cases have a hormone receptor positive subtype. Though this subtype has several options for treatment, the first-line therapies rely on sensitivity to alterations of estrogen signaling. Estrogen therapy resistance is common and will frequently develop over the treatment course, requiring progression of treatment intensity. Here, work surrounding the sigma-2 receptor pointing towards its involvement in endocrine therapy resistance is summarized, including the involvement of PI3K-mTOR signaling pathway and cholesterol metabolism. Though the identification of the sigma-2 receptor occurred decades ago, its gene was identified more recently, which has allowed for further exploration of its role in tumorigenesis and responses to treatments including endocrine therapy. Given its role in cholesterol homeostasis, particular interest regarding the sigma-2 receptor and estrogen-independent activation of the steroid receptor, estrogen receptor alpha, has been explored.
